kelvincornbread: Wendel "Mole" Kelvincornbr found a place in R-F17 between a snorer and a man who talked in his sleep. The available alternative was under the leak.
News that the Concord had taken Verdel Ridge reached Wendel "Mole" Kelvincornbr during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.
A recruit asked Wendel "Mole" Kelvincornbr how to write an address. He brought paper and began with the largest letters on a ration label.
noirangelfang: Tobias Noirangelfan arrived with the evening ration party, carrying his mother's thimble and a borrowed greatcoat two sizes too big.
Tobias Noirangelfan is always the first one awake. Today, under fire at Grey Mill, that habit was the only steady thing in S-F15.

Tobias Noirangelfan borrowed a book with three readers already waiting. For once, everyone was impatient about something other than relief. Verdel Ridge has been won. Tobias Noirangelfan listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch.
Dawn watch. Tobias Noirangelfan put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Edmund Potato, grazed.
smiridisnick: Zeno Smiridisnick reported to R-F15 with a bullet that missed him sewn into his tunic lining. The sergeant pretended not to notice.
Number 82 on the early rolls: Zeno Smiridisnick. The First Wave ribbon arrived with instructions about where to sew it and no needle.
Zeno Smiridisnick spent the afternoon delousing his shirt over a candle. The lice won on points.
News of the loss of Verdel Ridge reached R-F15 with the rations. Zeno Smiridisnick ate while listening to the revised orders.

The new recruit kept closing both eyes to aim. Zeno Smiridisnick spent the afternoon helping until one eye stayed open. Zeno Smiridisnick became a sapper today. He wrote the change in a letter home, then crossed out the explanation and tried again.
